To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the learning style and competency levels of learners affect their preferences and rating of different e-learning services.

1) the learning styles of students in the cohort are evenly spread across all the styles; 2) the competency levels of students are evenly spread across three levels; and 3) students with different learning styles and competency level have different preferences for e-learning services and personalization approaches.

the learning style and competency levels of engineering students undertaking computing courses in higher education have a significant impact on the preference of e-learning service and content personalisation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a context model for personalisation of e- learning services and content based upon learning styles and competency level.
the development of context-adaptive e- learning systems that can provide personalised e-learning content and services to learners of varying learning styles and competency level.
the following issues: (1) the context model for learner profile; (2) the learner profile based on learning styles and competency level; and (3) learner preferences of e-learning services.

the learning style and competency levels are important factors to be considered in the context of e-learning services personalisation and content adaptation.
the learning style and competency levels of the learner are important factors to consider in the design and development of e-learning systems and content.
the learning style of the learners and the competency level in the computing course have significant impact on their preference of e-learning services.
